title: The Eiffel Tower Rising Above the Champ de Mars
location_name: Eiffel Tower, Champ de Mars, Paris, France
case_note: A vast iron structure is taking shape beside a formal urban field prepared for an international exhibition.
historical_record: This press photograph records the Eiffel Tower during construction in 1888, one year before the Exposition Universelle opened. The incomplete iron lattice reveals how radically the tower differed from the masonry monuments that had defined the Paris skyline.
source: Bibliothèque nationale de France press photograph, Agence Mondial Photo-Presse
rights: Public domain archival photograph; source record and digital file supplied through the Bibliothèque nationale de France and Wikimedia Commons.
date_evidence: The BnF-linked file record identifies the photograph as a view of the Eiffel Tower's construction in 1888.
location_evidence: The surviving structure and the BnF title identify the construction site as the Eiffel Tower footprint on the Champ de Mars; the pin is placed on the tower itself.
image_evidence: The Commons file is a high-resolution reproduction of BnF record btv1b90502130 and names Agence Mondial Photo-Presse as the commissioning agency.

title: The Gare Saint-Lazare
case_note: Steam, iron roof trusses, and crowded platforms turn a transport interior into a modern urban landscape.
historical_record: Claude Monet painted the interior of Gare Saint-Lazare in 1877 as part of a group devoted to Paris's busiest railway terminus. Smoke and glass dissolve the station's engineering into atmosphere, making industrial movement itself a subject of modern painting.
rights: The 1877 painting is public domain. The National Gallery digital reproduction is made available as the source image represented on Wikimedia Commons.
date_evidence: The National Gallery catalogue dates Claude Monet's The Gare St-Lazare to 1877, and the Commons artwork record repeats that date.
location_evidence: The museum title and catalogue identify the depicted interior as Gare Saint-Lazare; the pin marks the station complex rather than Paris generally.
image_evidence: The high-resolution Commons file identifies National Gallery accession NG6479 and reproduces the same composition catalogued by the museum.

title: Tokyo Station at Completion
location_name: Tokyo Station Marunouchi Building, Tokyo, Japan
case_note: A long red-brick terminal announces a new metropolitan center at the edge of an imperial capital.
historical_record: The photograph shows Tokyo Station's original Marunouchi building immediately after its completion in 1914. Its red-brick facade joined long-distance rail travel to the governmental and commercial heart of Tokyo, becoming a symbol of Japan's modern transport network.
source: Published station-history scan reproduced by Wikimedia Commons
rights: Public domain in Japan and the United States under the old-photograph term described in the Commons rights record.
date_evidence: The file record identifies the view as the original Marunouchi station building immediately after completion in 1914 and cites a published history of Tokyo terminals.
location_evidence: The distinctive Marunouchi facade is identified in the source and survives on the west side of Tokyo Station; the coordinates mark that building.
image_evidence: The Commons scan is captioned as the complete front view of the original Tokyo Station building in 1914, not a later reconstruction photograph.

title: Sultan Ahmed Mosque and the Obelisk
case_note: A domed imperial mosque and an ancient obelisk share a ceremonial square at the meeting point of empires.
historical_record: Published in the Ottoman illustrated magazine Şehbal on 28 March 1912, this view places the Sultan Ahmed Mosque behind the Obelisk of Theodosius. The pairing compresses the Byzantine and Ottoman layers of the Hippodrome into one urban scene.
source: Şehbal magazine, 28 March 1912, reproduced through Wikimedia Commons
rights: Public domain: first published in the Ottoman Empire and identified by the Commons record as outside the former imperial copyright term.
date_evidence: The source record gives the magazine publication date as 28 March 1912 and identifies the subject in the contemporary caption.
location_evidence: Both the Sultan Ahmed Mosque and the Obelisk of Theodosius are visible, fixing the depicted place to Sultanahmet Square; the pin marks the mosque frontage.
image_evidence: The Commons file reproduces the Şehbal magazine image and retains the Ottoman publication and rights metadata.

title: The Taj Mahal from the Great Gate
location_name: Great Gate of the Taj Mahal, Agra, India
case_note: A monumental garden axis leads from a high gateway toward a white marble mausoleum beside a river.
historical_record: Dr. John Murray photographed this view from the roof of the Taj Mahal's entrance gate between January and March 1864. The elevated panorama records the garden before later planting changes and shows how the mausoleum was staged through symmetry, water, and distance.
source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gilman Collection, object 286084
rights: Public domain nineteenth-century photograph; the Metropolitan Museum record and Commons file identify the work as free of known copyright restrictions.
date_evidence: The Metropolitan Museum object record dates Murray's triptych to January-March 1864, establishing a single exact calendar year.
location_evidence: The museum description states that Murray photographed from the roof of the Taj Mahal entrance gate toward the mausoleum; the pin marks that Great Gate viewpoint.
image_evidence: The Commons image links directly to Met object 286084 and reproduces the museum's catalogued panorama.

title: Opening of the Sydney Harbour Bridge
case_note: Crowds gather on a new steel crossing whose opening alters the geography of a harbour city.
historical_record: Hall and Co. photographed the opening celebrations of the Sydney Harbour Bridge on 19 March 1932. The bridge joined the city's northern and southern shores by road and rail, while the mass gathering turned an engineering project into a civic ritual.
source: State Library of New South Wales, Home and Away collection, item 38540
rights: No known copyright restrictions/public-domain archival material as identified by the State Library-linked Commons record; attribution to the State Library of New South Wales is retained.
date_evidence: The State Library-linked record identifies the opening and the exposure date as 19 March 1932.
location_evidence: The source identifies the Sydney Harbour Bridge opening; the selected coordinates are the documented bridge-deck camera area used in the same Hall and Co. opening series.
image_evidence: The Commons file is a high-resolution copy from the State Library of New South Wales Hall and Co. nitrate-negative collection.

title: Boulder Dam Near Completion
location_name: Hoover Dam, Arizona-Nevada border, United States
case_note: Concrete, intake towers, and a steep desert gorge reveal a landscape being reorganized by federal engineering.
historical_record: A federal photographer recorded Boulder Dam from the Arizona side on 27 May 1935, as the structure neared completion. The dam transformed the Colorado River into a source of power, irrigation, and urban growth, while also remaking the river's ecology and regional politics.
source: U.S. National Archives / Herbert Hoover Presidential Library and Museum, record 31-AL21-244
rights: Public domain work of the United States federal government, confirmed by the National Archives-linked Commons record.
date_evidence: The federal archive caption dates the downstream view from the Arizona side to 27 May 1935 and supplies record number 31-AL21-244.
location_evidence: The archive caption names Boulder Dam and the Arizona-side viewpoint; the pin marks the dam wall at the state border.
image_evidence: The Commons file was uploaded from the Herbert Hoover Presidential Library and Museum's Hoover Dam collection with the federal record identifier.

title: The Hindenburg at Lakehurst
location_name: Hindenburg crash site, Naval Air Station Lakehurst, New Jersey, United States
case_note: A rigid airship meets a ground crew at a specialized landing field as a celebrated technology fails catastrophically.
historical_record: The Hindenburg caught fire while attempting to dock at Lakehurst on 6 May 1937. Photographs of the disaster circulated almost immediately and helped end public confidence in hydrogen-filled passenger airships, even though transatlantic aviation continued to expand.
source: Associated Press historical photograph reproduced through Wikimedia Commons; event site corroborated by the Lakehurst historic-site record
rights: The Commons record identifies the 1937 U.S. publication as public domain in the United States; owner should recheck international display implications before publication.
date_evidence: The image record identifies the Hindenburg disaster at Lakehurst on 6 May 1937, matching the documented event date.
location_evidence: The event occurred at the Lakehurst naval airship mooring field; the pin marks the registered crash site rather than the nearby town center.
image_evidence: The Commons record identifies the image as an Associated Press photograph of the Lakehurst disaster and supplies its publication history.

title: First Powered Flight at Kill Devil Hills
location_name: First Flight site, Kill Devil Hills, North Carolina, United States
case_note: A fragile machine leaves a launching rail over a wind-swept coastal field while one observer runs beside it.
historical_record: John T. Daniels exposed this plate at 10:35 a.m. on 17 December 1903 as Orville Wright made the first powered flight at Kill Devil Hills. The camera position, launching rail, and short flight path make the event unusually precise in both time and space.
source: Library of Congress, Wilbur and Orville Wright Papers, first-flight photograph
rights: Public domain photograph first published in the United States before 1929; Library of Congress source and Commons rights record supplied.
date_evidence: The Library of Congress identifies the exposure as the first flight at 10:35 a.m. on 17 December 1903.
location_evidence: The restored file records the camera position at the Kill Devil Hills launch site, and the Library of Congress account identifies the same coastal field.
image_evidence: The Commons restoration derives from the Library of Congress first-flight plate and preserves the original composition and attribution to John T. Daniels.

title: Allied Commanders at the Brandenburg Gate
case_note: Senior officers pass through a damaged monumental gate while a defeated capital is being divided among its occupiers.
historical_record: A British War Office photographer recorded Allied commanders at the Brandenburg Gate on 12 July 1945 after a decoration ceremony. The scene captures the brief public unity of the victorious powers at a landmark that would soon stand beside the boundary between East and West Berlin.
source: Imperial War Museums photograph TR 2913, War Office official photographer
rights: Public domain under expired United Kingdom Crown copyright, as stated in the Imperial War Museums-linked Commons record.
date_evidence: The Imperial War Museums caption dates photograph TR 2913 to 12 July 1945 and names the ceremony participants.
location_evidence: The archive caption explicitly places the ceremony at the Brandenburg Gate, which is visible behind the officers; the pin marks the gate.
image_evidence: The Commons file identifies Imperial War Museums collection number 4905-03 and photograph TR 2913 as its source.
